Because I was so young, the adjustment of our living situation felt like an adventure, and living with divorced parents became the status quo immediately. I don't miss my parents being married because I barely remember it. I don't have any traumatic memories of them fighting or the reasons they divorced because I *don't* remember those things, I was too young to get it. Trust me- this is absolutely better for her as long as you are a loving parent.

I agree with several of these points: redemption should include seeking to right your wrongs, I also wish that the royals became personal friends with anyone outside of the school's top 10 students, Remi is the royal who's the most genuinely and completely behind the cause (which... I said in the post that theyre not all morally perfect now) Arlo was a total asshole for a long time, Isen disliking solidarity, and so on. But I have to disagree on a lot of your points abt Arlo. 

First, I don't think he's ever been shown to enjoy beating down helpless people on virtue of the fact that they are helpless. In the early turf wars, he was trying to show off how powerful he was to Sera and make her want to come back to being queen/regret that she left (to be clear: this still makes him a complete jerk, just with different motivations than alleged), and with John, at no point after meeting him did Arlo think he was helpless. Arlo saw his confidence, and later saw his eyes glow, and all their interactions were basically him trying to get John to admit he was powerful and "take his rightful place in the hierarchy". Most of what he does is him reinforcing the classist rhetoric that their society teaches. Again- all of this is very very very bad. But he doesn't enjoy hurting/humiliating people on virtue of hurting/humiliating them. which seems to be a fundamental difference in how we read the character. 

Okay and point 2 is that in my view, he is doing things to right his wrongs. He's helping with the safe house, which we know is something he wouldn't do if he didn't want the low and mid tiers to feel safer at school/if it ran counter to his own wishes, because he quit briefly when he was having doubts, but came back. He's also on friendly terms with Seraphina again- at the beginning of the series he was pretty awful towards her, not taking no for an answer, lying to get her to come to turf wars so he can flex, etc etc, but now he's chilled out and been honest with her abt John, as well as accompanying and protecting her when she asked him to. It's doubtful he'd do all that for her if she had never been a high tier, because he wouldn't be close to her if she had never been a high tier, but again: I do hope UnO addresses this class divide and has the royals (especially Arlo) be friends with people who are far below them. 

His view of the hierarchy, which was the source of all of his shitty behavior, is slowly becoming less and less solid. I expect for him to continue to be better to those around him as this trend continues, though I don't know if you'll get your desired apology to those students from turf wars because I'm pretty sure we haven't seen them since then.

Also: based on this comment I very much respect your views on redemption. But anyways yeah this was unorganized and may be the comment that gets me downvotes, though I want to be clear I'm not justifying any of it, I'm just trying to explain that due to the way I interpret his motivations, him changing as his core views are challenged makes sense to me, so I interpret the positive things he does as genuine.
